title: Event pipeline: Kafka vs SQS
brief: An API publishes 2k events/s; 30 workers (200 events/s each) process them. Side A sends them through Kafka with 12 partitions; side B through a standard SQS queue. Same workers on both. Decide which you'd run, and what you'd change on each.

scenarios.label: Steady 2k events/s
scenarios.about: Both keep up. Compare the cost row: Kafka is billed per broker-hour, SQS per request.

scenarios.label: Traffic doubles
scenarios.about: At 10 s events double to 4k/s. There are 30 workers on both sides. How many can actually work on each?

scenarios.label: Workers down 10 s
scenarios.about: The workers crash at 10 s and come back at 20 s. Events keep arriving. How fast does each side drain the backlog?

questions: Why do 30 workers drain faster from SQS than from 12 Kafka partitions? What would you change in Kafka?
At what event rate does Kafka's flat price beat SQS's per-request price?
Which side lets a new consumer replay last week's events? Which keeps events in order?
SQS delivers at least once. What must the workers do about duplicates?
hints: In the growth scenario, how many workers are busy on each side?
A Kafka partition is read by one consumer per group. With 12 partitions, workers 13 to 30 sit idle. SQS lets every worker take messages.

Kafka needs more partitions (20+) to use 30 workers, and is far cheaper at a steady 2k/s. SQS scales consumers freely but costs per message (batching would cut that up to 10x). Kafka keeps events for replay and orders them per partition; standard SQS does neither.
_notes: Graph: client -> api (10 x 1k) -> events -> worker (30 x 200/s, $0.10 each). Kafka: 12 partitions, drain = min(30, 12) x 200 = 2.4k/s; $0.63/hr (3 MSK brokers). SQS: drain 30 x 200 = 6k/s; $1.20 per million messages (send + receive + delete, unbatched). Sim cost at 2k/s: Kafka $4.63 vs SQS $12.64/hr (workers $3 + api $1 on both). Growth to 4k/s: Kafka backlog grows 1.6k/s (48k at 40 s), SQS keeps up ($19.29/hr). Outage 10-20 s: both build 20k; SQS drains at 4k/s (done in ~5 s), Kafka at 400/s (4k left at 60 s). Client latency is the same on both: the queue decouples it. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
